Health and safety · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Near-miss report prioritization

Pedro · EHS Analyst

A distribution center with 780 operators, 42 forklifts and 3 shifts receives about 260 near-miss reports a month, between the app and paper cards.

When it runs
Every Friday at 2 p.m., before the CIPA's weekly Monday meeting, with the reports received in the app and the cards typed in during the week
What it delivers in production
Every Friday at 3 p.m. the technician and the CIPA get the ranking of areas and risk types, the spots with repeated reports, the high severity reports and the comparison with the PGR inventory.
Who decides
Classifies and ranks; the CIPA decides
Effort
Calibrate on 200 reports; two weeks
Set up5 steps · 7 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

# Risk matrix, PGR inventory and DC map

PGR is the risk management program required by Brazilian workplace safety standard NR-1. CIPA is the internal accident prevention committee. CAT is the work accident report.

## Potential severity (PGR 5 x 5 matrix, consequence axis)
Use the worst plausible outcome of the type. Do not change the table.
| Type | Worst plausible outcome | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| pedestrian strike | death of a pedestrian | 5 |
| fall from height | death or disability | 5 |
| falling load | serious injury with time off work | 4 |
| chemical | severe burn | 4 |
| collision | moderate injury | 3 |
| crushing | moderate injury | 3 |
| behavior | moderate injury | 3 |
| ergonomics | minor injury | 2 |
| PPE | minor injury | 2 |
A forklift that passes close to or nearly touches a person on foot is a pedestrian strike. A vehicle against a structure or another vehicle is a collision.

## Area map (standard name and how it appears in reports)
- Dock 7 x Street C crossing: "dock 7 crossing", "dock 7 and Street C"
- Dock 2 | Street C | Picking mezzanine | Battery area (charging)

## PGR inventory by area
| Area | Inventoried risks |
|---|---|
| Dock 7 x Street C crossing | pedestrian strike, collision |
| Dock 2 | pedestrian strike, PPE, ergonomics |
| Street C | collision, pedestrian strike, behavior |
| Picking mezzanine | falling load, fall from height, ergonomics |
| Battery area | ergonomics, crushing |

## Count and ranking
- Ranking: the area's maximum severity first; on a tie, more consecutive weeks of the dominant type. Never by quantity.
- Repetition: consecutive weeks with the same type in the same area, counting the current one. No history: new.
- A report with an injury that happened: POSSIBLE ACCIDENT, outside the table and the count by area; it enters only the header total.

## Rules with no leeway
- Name, employee number and badge do not appear anywhere in the output. The footer gives only the quantity. E.g.: C-201 has 1 identification removed.
- Area and type by the text, with the change recorded. E.g.: 3101 marked Dock 2 and PPE becomes Dock 7 x Street C crossing and pedestrian strike.
- Ranking: E.g.: Dock 2 has 3 reports and comes last (severity 2); Mezzanine (4, 2 weeks) comes before Battery area (4, new).
- Arithmetic: 14 reports (10 from the app, 4 on cards); night with 7 of 14 (50%); convex mirror open for 39 days on Nov 13.
- POSSIBLE ACCIDENT: E.g.: 3109 (cut with a visit to the clinic) goes to the safety technician to assess a CAT and stays outside the table.
- No blame: do not write blame, negligence or operator failure, not even for the phone use in 3110. Describe condition, place and behavior.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The reporter is never identified: the agent receives no name, employee ID or badge and removes from the summary any sentence that points to who reported or who committed the deviation, because a report that turns into punishment kills the program. The agent does not blame operators; it describes condition, location and behavior. Severity comes from the PGR matrix, and every report rated 4 or 5 goes through the technician before the CIPA. A report with an injury that occurred becomes POSSIBLE ACCIDENT and goes to the technician the same day to assess the CAT (work accident report).

Common mistakes

  • Prioritizing by quantity: 11 reports of a forgotten vest jump ahead of 4 near-fatal collisions.
  • Reading the type marked by the reporter as final; 'behavior' is often a bad layout, and the engineering action is different.
  • Treating a drop in reports in an area as improvement, and not as fear of reporting after a warning.
  • Discussing only the week's reports at the CIPA; repetition over 4 weeks at the same spot is the strongest signal.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Reports read and classified per weekfrom about 30% to all reports opened in the weekestimate based on the described routine
Weeks between the first repeated report at a spot and the CIPA discussionfrom months to 1 to 2 weeksestimate based on the described routine
CIPA serious reports in the top 10 positions of the ranking100% in the 200 calibration reports, the acceptance criterionestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Reports for week 35 of 2026: 63, of which 48 through the app and 15 on cards. Night shift: 41%.
Area | Dominant type | Reports | Maximum severity (matrix) | Repetition vs 4 weeks
Dock 7 x aisle C crossing | forklift and pedestrian collision | 9 | 4 | 4th week in a row, 27 reports accumulated
Picking mezzanine | object falling from a shelf | 7 | 3 | up
Battery area | chemical, leak during charging | 3 | 4 | new
Dock 2 | PPE, no reflective vest | 11 | 2 | stable
SEVERITY 4 OR 5 REPORTS for the CIPA to read: 4 reports, ids 2201, 2207, 2219 and 2240, with no reporter identification.
PGR inventory: the battery charging leak is not listed for the area; suggest a review to the safety engineer.
Actions in progress: convex mirror at dock 7, open for 38 days, no status.
